content.title: About
content.content: Turkey breakfast links are tender, lightly seasoned sausages made from ground turkey, salt, spices, and sometimes a touch of sugar. Sold raw, they require cooking before consumption and are intended for quick morning meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey contains less saturated fat than traditional pork breakfast sausage.
Breakfast links are shaped into small, bite‑size links for fast cooking.
The mild version uses a modest amount of spices, making it kid‑friendly.
Raw links have a brighter turkey flavor but must be fully cooked to eliminate pathogens.
They are typically pan‑fried or microwaved for 3‑5 minutes.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Turkey provides high‑quality protein with less total fat than pork, supporting a leaner diet.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A typical serving (≈ 3 oz) delivers about 15 g of complete protein for muscle maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey breakfast links contain niacin (B3), vitamin B6, and folate, which aid metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Selenium, zinc, and phosphorus are present, contributing to immune function and bone health.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Raw turkey links usually provide around 120 kcal per 100 g, helpful for weight management.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Raw poultry can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter, so the product must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to turkey meat.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Processed sausage often contains added salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands add nitrites for color stability, which some consumers prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the links until they reach an internal temperature of 74 °C – pan‑fry, boil, or bake. Serve with eggs, toast, vegetables, or in a breakfast sandwich.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw links refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in their original packaging for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months. Discard if an off‑odor develops.
